contexts.used_clause:
1. for every $\theta$ with $0<\theta<1$ the series
   $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha(z-a)^\alpha$ converges absolutely and uniformly on
   $\overline\Delta_{\theta r}(a)$, so its sum $g$ is defined on
   $\Delta_r(a)$;
2. $g$ is holomorphic on $\Delta_r(a)$, with
   $$Dg(z)h=\sum_{k<m}b_k(z)h_k,\qquad b_k(z)=\sum_{\alpha}\alpha_k\,c_\alpha(z-a)^{\alpha-e_k},$$
   the $k$th series running over the multi-indices with $\alpha_k\ge1$ and
   converging absolutely on $\Delta_r(a)$; equivalently
   $\partial_{z_k}g=b_k$;
premise_quotes: [F7] A coefficient family with a bound $|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{i=1}^n r_i^{-\alpha_i}$ defines a holomorphic sum on the open polydisc of positive radii $r_i$. Its coefficients are its derivatives at the origin divided by the corresponding factorials. If $c,c':\mathbb N^n\to\mathbb C$ satisfy $|c_\alpha|\le M\prod_{i=1}^n r_i^{-\alpha_i}$ and $|c'_\alpha|\le M'\prod_{i=1}^n r_i^{-\alpha_i}$ for positive radii $r_i$, and their sums agree on the corresponding open polydisc, then $c_\alpha=c'_\alpha$ for every $\alpha$ ([[lem-qftx-bounded-power-series-holomorphy-and-coefficient-uniqueness]]).
